Let me analyze this OIML certificate.

Certificate details:
- Issuing Authority: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB)
- Address: Bundesallee 100, 38116 Braunschweig
- Person responsible: Dr. O. Mack
- Title: Head of Working Group
- Certificate No.: R76/1992-DE1-98.04, Revision 4
- Member State: Germany
- Date issued: 04.09.2013 (dates at signatures)

Applicant: Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG, Weender Landstr. 94-108, 37075 Göttingen, Germany
Manufacturer: same as applicant ("Manufacturer of the certified type is the applicant.")

Also mentioned: certificate transferred from old owner Sartorius AG to new owner Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG. The applicant is the new owner.

Certified type:
- Category: Nonautomatic weighing instrument (NAWI) → "Weighing instrument" or "Nonautomatic weighing instrument". The schema examples: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", ... I'll use "Nonautomatic weighing instrument".
- Type designations: BD BH 110, DS BH 310, DT BH 210, DT BH 310
- Description: "The weighing instrument consists of a weighing platform with one load cell of electromagnetic force compensation (class I) or one strain-gauge load cell (class II and III) and of an incorporated indicating device for displaying the weighing results, and of a keypad to operate the instrument."

Recommendation: R76-1, edition 1992, Amendment 1 (1994), accuracy classes I, II, III.

Test reports: report No. 1.12-4010127 and associated test reports No. 1.12-4010127/1, /2, /3, /4. Former test reports 1.14-98.281, 1.14-99017618, 1.14-00021194 remain valid.

Revision history: Revision 4 — the certificate is a revision 4; date 04.09.2013. Changes: transfer of certificate from Sartorius AG to Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG. I'll include revision_history: [{revision: "4", date: "2013-09-04", changes: "Transfer of the certificate from Sartorius AG to Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG"}].

Model family: 4 models: BD BH 110, DS BH 310, DT BH 210, DT BH 310.

Table 1 characteristics per model:

BD BH 110: Class (I); weighing pan size ≤ Ø80mm or Ø90mm; Max 50...210g; e = 1mg...2mg; d = 0.1mg...2mg; n ≤ 210000; Temperature +15°C/+25°C; Nominal capacity of load receptor 252g; Initial zero setting + dead load ≤ 202g.

DS BH 310: Class (III); pan ≤ 147x178mm or Ø150mm; Max 500...1200g; e = 1g...2g; d = 1g...2g; n ≤ 1200; Temp +10°C/+40°C; Nominal capacity 1500g; Initial zero setting + dead load ≤ 1000g.

DT BH 210: Class (II); pan ≤ Ø116mm; Max 500...510g; e = 0.1g; d = 0.01g; n ≤ 5100; Temp +10°C/+30°C; Nominal capacity 610g; Initial zero ≤ 110g.

DT BH 310: Class (III); pan ≤ Ø116mm; Max 50...120g; e = 0.1g...0.2g; d = 0.1g...0.2g; n ≤ 1200; Temp +10°C/+40°C; Nominal capacity 610g; Initial zero ≤ 560g.

Tare-balancing range ≤ 100% of Max (all models, type-level).

Footnote 1: "The sum of Max, initial zero-setting range and the dead load shall not exceed the nominal capacity of the load receptor." — applies to nominal capacity of load receptor.

Now handle units: Max 50...210g → value {min: 50, max: 210}, unit "g". e = 1mg...2mg → {min: 1, max: 2}, unit "mg". d = 0.1mg...2mg → {min: 0.1, max: 2}, unit "mg". Note that some ranges mix? No, they're consistent units within each model. But across models in model_level, units differ per model (BD BH 110 e in mg, DS BH 310 e in g). Hmm, model_level values structure: {model, value, footnote_markers[]} — no unit per value in schema. The schema example shows unit_symbol at attribute level. But values have different units per model here. Options: normalize to one unit (e.g., convert mg to g: 1mg = 0.001g) or set unit per value... The schema's model_level: {attribute, unit, values[]: {model, value, footnote_markers[]}}. Values don't carry unit. To be safe, I could normalize all mass values to grams. E.g., maximum_capacity: BD BH 110 {min:50,max:210} g; DS BH 310 {min:500,max:1200} g; DT BH 210 {min:500,max:510} g; DT BH 310 {min:50,max:120} g — all in g already.

e (verification scale interval): BD BH 110: 1mg...2mg = {min: 0.001, max: 0.002} g; DS BH 310: {min:1, max:2} g; DT BH 210: 0.1 g; DT BH 310: {min:0.1, max:0.2} g. Normalize to g. unit_symbol "g".

d (actual scale interval): BD BH 110: 0.1mg...2mg = {min: 0.0001, max: 0.002} g; DS BH 310: {min:1,max:2} g; DT BH 210: 0.01 g; DT BH 310: {min:0.1,max:0.2} g.

n ≤ (number of verification scale intervals): 210000, 1200, 5100, 1200. Dimensionless. Could express as {min:null, max: 210000}? The rule: "≤210000" → {min: null, max: 210000}. I'll do that, unit null.

Class: accuracy class per model — could be a model_level attribute "accuracy_class" with values "I", "III", "II", "III". String values fine.

Weighing pan size: BD BH 110: Ø80mm or Ø90mm (two options); DS BH 310: 147x178mm or Ø150mm; DT BH 210: Ø116mm; DT BH 210/310: Ø116mm. These are string-ish values with dimensions. Value as string "Ø80 mm or Ø90 mm"? Since it's two alternatives. Value can be a string. Unit symbol mm? The value is like "Ø80 mm or Ø90 mm". I'd store value as string, unit_symbol "mm". Or split min/max? Not really a range. I'll store value: "Ø80 mm or Ø90 mm", unit_symbol: "mm". Attribute: maximum_weighing_pan_size. Actually "Weighing pan size ≤" — max pan size. Value strings with Ø.

Hmm, but strict rule: numbers not strings where numeric. Pan size isn't a simple number (diameter vs rectangle), so string is appropriate.

Temperature range: BD BH 110: +15/+25 °C; DS BH 310: +10/+40 °C; DT BH 210: +10/+30 °C; DT BH 310: +10/+40 °C.

Nominal capacity of load receptor: 252g, 1500g, 610g, 610g. Footnote marker 1).

Initial zero setting + dead load ≤: 202g, 1000g, 110g, 560g. {min:null, max: value}.

Tare-balancing range ≤ 100% of Max — type_level: value 100, unit "%", maybe reference "Max". Could add tare_balancing_reference: "Max". I'll do value: 100, unit_symbol: "%".

matrix_tables: include Table 1 as matrix table too. The R137 example populates matrix_tables AND model_level. I'll include matrix_tables with Table 1.

Components: "weighing platform with one load cell of electromagnetic force compensation (class I) or one strain-gauge load cell (class II and III) and incorporated indicating device and keypad". Could record components: load cell (alternatives OR), indicating device (incorporated), keypad. No type designations given. I'll include components with roles.

Also weighing ranges chosen within limits of No. 3.2 of R 76-1 and Table 1.

certificate fields:
- number: "R76/1992-DE1-98.04"
- scheme: "A"? PTB issues under OIML-CS... Actually this is 1992 R76 certificate, before OIML-CS. But the schema requires scheme A|B. Hmm — OIML-CS scheme A is for R76. The certificate number format R76/1992-DE1-98.04 — DE1 indicates PTB as issuer. I'll set scheme "A".
- project_number: not present. Omit or null. Maybe "98.04"? No, that's part of cert number. Omit.
- page_total: 3
- member_state: "Germany"
- date_issued: "2013-09-04"
- oiml_issuer_id: maybe "DE1"? The cert number contains DE1. Not explicitly stated elsewhere. I could include "DE1" as inferred... Rule 8: don't fabricate. The "DE1" appears in the certificate number. Hmm. I'll omit oiml_issuer_id or set null? Safer to omit since not explicitly given. Actually the pattern "DE1" in cert numbers is the OIML issuer code. But it's not labeled. I'll omit to be safe. Actually I think including "DE1" extracted from the number is reasonable but risky. I'll omit.

issuing_authority:
- name: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt
- address_lines: ["Bundesallee 100", "38116 Braunschweig"]
- person_responsible: "Dr. O. Mack"
- person_title: "Head of Working Group"
- oiml_issuer_id: omit or null.

applicants: [{name: "Sartorius Lab Instruments GmbH & Co. KG", address_lines: ["Weender Landstr. 94-108", "37075 Göttingen", "Germany"]}]

manufacturers: same (manufacturer of certified type is the applicant).

certified_type:
- category: "Nonautomatic weighing instrument"
- type_designations: ["BD BH 110", "DS BH 310", "DT BH 210", "DT BH 310"]
- module_designation: "Not applicable"? The instrument includes load cells and indicating device — it's a complete instrument. The R76 context: module designation not mentioned. Set null or omit. I'll omit... Actually schema wants module_designation field. I'll set null.
- description: "Nonautomatic electromechanical weighing instrument. The weighing instrument consists of a weighing platform with one load cell of electromagnetic force compensation (class I) or one strain-gauge load cell (class II and III) and of an incorporated indicating device for displaying the weighing results, and of a keypad to operate the instrument."

model_family:
- family_name: null
- models: [{model_id: "BD BH 110"}, {model_id: "DS BH 310"}, {model_id: "DT BH 210"}, {model_id: "DT BH 310"}]

components:
- {role: "load_cell", type_designations: [], alternatives: "OR", characteristics: {type_level: {...}}? } Hmm, the schema says characteristics{} — sub-characteristics. The load cells: electromagnetic force compensation (class I) OR strain-gauge (class II and III). No type designations. I'll include:
  - {role: "weighing_platform", type_designations: []}
  - {role: "load_cell", type_designations: [], alternatives: "OR", characteristics: {"technology options": ...}} — maybe simpler: characteristics: {"force_compensation": "electromagnetic force compensation (class I) or strain gauge (class II and III)"}. Keep light.
  - {role: "indicating_device", type_designations: [], characteristics: {"incorporated": true}}
  - {role: "keypad", ...}

Maybe simpler to just include load_cell, indicating_device, keypad. Weighing platform too. I'll include all four but keep minimal.

characteristics:
type_level:
- tare_balancing_range: {value: {min: null, max: 100}, unit_symbol: "%"} with reference? Actually "Tare-balancing range ≤ 100% of Max". I could add "tare_balancing_reference": {"value": "Max"}. Or value "100% of Max" as string. Better: value {min:null, max:100}, unit "%", plus separate note. Keep simple.

model_level:
- accuracy_class: values I/III/II/III (strings). unit null.
- maximum_capacity (Max): ranges per model, unit "g".
- verification_scale_interval_e: per model, unit "g" (normalize mg→g).
- actual_scale_interval_d: per model, unit "g".
- max_number_of_verification_scale_intervals_n: {min:null,max:X}, unit null.
- weighing_pan_size: strings, unit "mm".
- temperature_range: {min, max}, unit "°C".
- nominal_capacity_of_load_receptor: number, unit "g", footnote_markers ["1)"].
- initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load: {min:null, max:X}, unit "g".

Wait — footnote markers per value in model_level values: {model, value, footnote_markers[]}. Good, nominal capacity values get footnote_markers: ["1)"].

Hmm, unit per value: since I normalize to g, attribute-level unit_symbol "g" works.

Actually wait: for temperature range values in model_level — values are objects {min, max}, unit at attribute level "°C". Fine.

matrix_tables: Table 1:
name: "Table 1 – Weighing ranges and characteristics per type"
columns: ["type", "class", "weighing_pan_size_max", "max", "e", "d", "n_max", "tare_balancing_range_max", "temperature_range", "load_receptor_nominal_capacity", "initial_zero_setting_plus_dead_load_max"]
rows: per type.

I'll include units within row values as-is? The R137 example had column_units. I'll add column_units where applicable: [null, null, "mm", "g", "g", "g", null, "%", "°C", "g", "g"]. But pan size strings contain mm; and values mixing mg/g in raw form. In matrix table rows, I could preserve raw strings to be faithful, e.g. "50...210 g". Hmm, but rule says numbers not strings. For matrix_tables, the example R137 uses numbers. I'll normalize: e and d converted to grams.

BD BH 110: class "(Ⅰ)" → "I"; pan "Ø80 mm or Ø90 mm"; max {min:50,max:210}; e {min:0.001,max:0.002}; d {min:0.0001,max:0.002}; n {min:null,max:210000}; tare {min:null,max:100}; temp {min:15,max:25}; capacity 252; initial zero {min:null,max:202}.
DS BH 310: class "III"; pan "147x178 mm or Ø150 mm"; max {500,1200}; e {1,2}; d {1,2}; n ≤1200; temp {10,40}; capacity 1500; zero 1000.

DT BH 310: class "III"; pan "Ø116 mm"; max {50,120}; e {0.1,0.2}; d {0.1,0.2}; n ≤1200; temp {10,40}; capacity 610; zero 560.

- id: "R76" (canonical). edition: 1992, amendment: "1 (1994)" or "Amendment 1 (1994)". The cert says "R76-1, edition 1992, including Amendment 1 (1994)". The recommendation is R76 (R76-1 is the part for metrological requirements). Canonical id "R76", edition 1992, amendment "1 (1994)" — hmm amendment as string. accuracy_classes: ["I","II","III"].
- scheme: "A".

Hmm, the changes description is inferred — the document indeed describes the transfer. Reasonable.

certificate.number: "R76/1992-DE1-98.04". 

Should certificate include oiml_issuer_id "DE1"? I'll include "DE1" — it's part of the number and is the PTB OIML issuer code. Risky per rule 8. I'll leave it out. Actually... many extractors would include it. The instruction: "If a field is not present in the markdown, omit it." The "DE1" is present in the number but not as a labeled field. I'll omit.

date_issued: the signature dates are 04.09.2013. That's when revision 4 was signed. I'll use "2013-09-04".

Description of weighing ranges choice: "The weighing ranges with Max, Min, e, d and number of verification scale intervals may be chosen within the limits of No. 3.2 of R 76-1 and of the table 1." Include in description or as type_level characteristic? I'll fold into certified_type.description.

Model-level attribute naming:

Units for e/d normalized to g. But wait — should I keep mg for BD BH 110? The unit_symbol at attribute level. Normalizing to g is cleaner and correct numerically. 0.1 mg = 0.0001 g. d for BD BH 110: 0,1mg...2mg → {min: 0.0001, max: 0.002}. OK.

Weighing pan size values: "Ø80 mm or Ø90 mm", "147 x 178 mm or Ø150 mm", "Ø116 mm", "Ø116 mm". unit_symbol "mm". Note rule 2 says pure units aren't values, but these strings contain dimension info, fine.

Now accuracy_class values: "(Ⅰ)" — Roman numerals as unicode chars Ⅰ Ⅱ Ⅲ. Use "I", "II", "III" ASCII. Good.

Type-level characteristics: tare_balancing_range: {value: {min: null, max: 100}, unit_symbol: "%"}. Maybe add "tare_balancing_range_reference": {"value": "Max"}? I'll skip; instead keep it simple. Hmm, but "100% of Max" — I could make value "100% of Max" string, but rules prefer structured. Keep {max:100} "%" and note in description? Fine.

Also "weighing ranges ... may be chosen within the limits of No. 3.2 of R 76-1" — could add type_level characteristic "weighing_range_flexibility": {"value": "Max, Min, e, d and number of verification scale intervals may be chosen within the limits of No. 3.2 of R 76-1 and Table 1"}. I'll include as a note? It's descriptive; I'll fold into description.
